name: Alabama
typical: Admits cluster around students with 24+ college hours and a solid C-plus-to-B record; the stated floor is only a 2.0 overall on all university-level work, so the 51% rate reflects a large and self-selecting out-of-state applicant pool rather than a hard academic screen. Under 24 hours you must also satisfy first-time first-year admission requirements.
levers: If coming from an Alabama Community College System school, file a STARS (Statewide Transfer and Articulation Reporting System) articulation guide for your major. It functions as a contract that the completed gen-ed core transfers and applies to UA degree requirements.

Use UA's unusually permissive grade rule: transferable courses with a D- or above may apply to degree requirements. Only EN 101, EN 102 and MATH 100/110/112/113/115 require a C- or better, so a couple of weak non-gateway grades will not sink an application the way they would elsewhere.
watchouts: UA sets no cap on total transferred hours, but at least 50% of the coursework for the bachelor's must be earned at a four-year institution and 25% at UA itself. Community college credit beyond roughly half the degree will transfer onto the transcript without applying to the degree.
Competitive programs, notably Capstone College of Nursing and parts of business, admit separately and well above the 2.0 university floor.
feeders: Shelton State Community College in Tuscaloosa is the closest and largest pipeline, alongside Jefferson State, Calhoun, Wallace State, and Bevill State in the ACCS. UA also draws an unusually large share of out-of-state transfers relative to peers, particularly

name: American
typical: Verified D2: 713 applied, 654 admitted, 127 enrolled. A 91.7% transfer admit rate is unusually high and is not a typo — AU admits nearly every transfer applicant who clears the bar, then converts only 19.4% of them. The real gate is the stated 2.5 college GPA and good standing at all prior schools; denials cluster below that line. Required: college transcripts, essay, statement of good standing. Test scores not required; high school transcript only recommended of some. Treat AU as an access school for transfers, not a reach, and negotiate on price and credit rather than on odds.
levers: American Transfer Advantage: 30+ credits from an accredited community college, a 3.0 GPA, a filed FAFSA, admission, and a transfer advising meeting yields up to 50% tuition support. Fall priority is May 1, and Phi Theta Kappa members get priority consideration. Dual-enrolled students are excluded.

Because admission is near-automatic at 2.5+, put the effort into credit placement instead of the pitch: AU accepts up to 75 credits from a two-year institution, but only courses graded C (2.0) or better transfer, so re-take or re-sequence anything below a C before you apply.
watchouts: AU caps transfer credit at 75 and requires 45 credits completed in residence, so arriving with 90 credits still leaves roughly three semesters of full tuition.
On-campus housing is space-available and gives preference to students admitted with 36 or fewer credits — junior-level transfers should budget for DC off-campus rent from day one.
feeders: AU publishes no feeder-school list. It recruits community college students nationally rather than regionally, with Phi Theta Kappa chapters as the named national channel and the DMV two-years — Montgomery College, Northern Virginia Community College, Prince Ge

name: Arizona
typical: Roughly two out of three transfer applicants are admitted, on a rolling basis. The CDS floor is 12 transferable credits and a 2.00 college GPA, with only C-or-better coursework transferring — the real screening happens inside majors like Eller, Nursing and Engineering, not at the university gate.
levers: Complete the AGEC (Arizona General Education Curriculum, ~35 lower-division units) at an Arizona community college — UA accepts it as satisfying its lower-division gen ed: composition, math, Exploring Perspectives, Building Connections and required attributes, so you arrive with gen ed closed out.

For Eller: students who meet the published Professional Admission eligibility requirements are guaranteed admission to the Business Management Professional major on Main Campus. The Professional Admission window for a fall start is January-February, separate from the university transfer application.
watchouts: CDS D13 caps transfer credit from a two-year college at 64 semester credits, and D12 says only grades of C or higher move — credits banked past 64 at a community college are dead weight, and D16 still requires 30 credits completed at UA for the bachelor's.

The ~66% figure is the university-wide rate. Eller, Nursing and Engineering run their own major-level admission with higher bars, so admission to Arizona is not admission to the major you applied for.
feeders: Arizona community colleges dominate: Pima CC (Eller publishes a dedicated Pima transfer guide) and the Maricopa district colleges (Mesa, Glendale, Phoenix, Scottsdale, Chandler-Gilbert), routed through AZTransfer/AGEC. Secondary flow from California community

name: Arizona State
typical: Effectively criteria-based rather than competitive: 6,865 of 7,572 transfer applicants were admitted and 3,749 enrolled. CDS D4/D8 set the bar plainly — at least 12 completed semester credits, and a college GPA of 2.0 for Arizona residents or 2.5 for nonresidents. If you clear those, you are very likely admitted to the university; the real screening happens at the major level.
levers: Complete the Arizona General Education Curriculum (AGEC-A/B/S) or a transferable associate degree at an Arizona community college and use MyPath2ASU, ASU's free course-by-course transfer map covering 300+ partner colleges — it locks your credits to a specific ASU major and preserves junior standing instead of transferring credits piecemeal.

Use spring or summer entry as a second door: CDS D3 shows ASU admits transfers in fall, spring and summer on rolling admission, and D13/D14 allow up to 64 semester hours from a two-year college with unlimited hours from four-year institutions, so a semester of repair work at a community college does not cost you time.
watchouts: The 90.7% is a university-level number and does not get you your major. Barrett Honors College, W. P. Carey (business), Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering and Edson nursing run their own transfer GPA and prerequisite screens — admitted students are routinely placed in an exploratory or alternate major instead.

This CDS is for ASU Campus Immersion (the physical campuses) only; ASU Online files a separate CDS, so do not apply this rate to the online degrees. Also note nonresidents face a 2.5 GPA minimum versus 2.0 for Arizona residents.
feeders: Overwhelmingly the Maricopa County Community College District (Mesa, Glendale, Phoenix, Scottsdale, Chandler-Gilbert, Rio Salado) plus Pima CC in Tucson, layered on top of a national MyPath2ASU partner network of 300+ colleges that feeds a large out-of-state transfer flow.

name: Auburn
typical: The typical admit is an Alabama Community College System student with 30+ transferable hours and roughly a 3.0, comfortably above Auburn's 2.5 floor, applying into a non-impacted major. Auburn admits to the major, so the 58.5% university-wide rate overstates odds for engineering, nursing, and architecture applicants who face a second screen.
levers: File an Alabama STARS (Statewide Transfer and Articulation Reporting System) guide before finishing at an ACCS two-year college. STARS produces a binding articulation contract that locks in which gen-ed courses transfer and apply to your Auburn major, so credit is not re-litigated at evaluation.

Cross the 24-semester-hour line and finish the major's pre-professional sequence before applying. Under 24 hours Auburn reviews you as an entering first-year student, putting your high school record back in play; with the pre-req core done (e.g. Calc I/II, chem, physics for Ginn engineering) you compete as a prepared major applicant rather than a general transfer.
watchouts: Auburn requires 25% of degree requirements be completed in residence at Auburn, so piling up community college hours past that point does not shorten time to degree.

The published 2.5 cumulative GPA is a university floor, not the bar for limited-enrollment programs. Engineering, nursing, and architecture/design screen well above it, and admission to Auburn is not admission to the major.
feeders: Heaviest inflow from adjacent Alabama Community College System campuses, especially Southern Union State (Opelika/Wadley), Chattahoochee Valley, Jefferson State, Gadsden State, and Calhoun. Meaningful secondary flow from west Georgia two-year and four-year sch

name: Baylor
typical: CDS D2: 1,678 applied, 1,514 admitted, 355 enrolled (23% yield). The 90% admit rate is real but reflects a pre-filtered pool: Baylor's own CDS states a 2.75 college GPA is the floor it will consider, you must be eligible to return to every prior institution, and applicants under 24 completed hours must also submit a high school transcript. Standardized tests are not required. The people who get in are Texas community college students (heavily McLennan) and in-state four-year transfers who clear 2.75+, are in good standing everywhere, and are transferring by the end of sophomore year.
levers: Baylor Bound with McLennan Community College: enroll full-time at MCC, follow a Baylor-MCC Degree MAP, and hold a 2.5 GPA for guaranteed Baylor admission plus MCC-specific transfer scholarships. It is the only published guaranteed-admission pathway into Baylor, and it lowers the GPA bar below the 2.75 CDS floor.

Transfer no later than end of sophomore year and time it to the June 15 fall priority date. Baylor reviews on rolling admission (CDS D9) with fall 6/15, spring 11/15, and summer 5/15 priority dates, so a spring entry is a genuine second door rather than a consolation prize.
watchouts: Credit math, not admission, is the real risk: Baylor caps two-year college transfer credit at 70 hours (D13) and requires 60 hours in residence including the last 30 (D16 and Baylor's own D11 note). Arriving with 80+ community college hours means paying for credits that cannot shorten the degree.

Baylor's CDS D11 says outright that some majors carry academic requirements above the 2.75 minimum, and that you must be eligible to return to any college previously attended. A withdrawal-heavy or probation record blocks admission regardless of GPA.
feeders: Baylor publishes no ranked feeder list. The documented pipeline is McLennan Community College in Waco, via both the Baylor Bound agreement and the invite-only MCC Start program for students Baylor redirects from first-year admission. Beyond MCC, the realistic

name: Binghamton
typical: About 44% admitted (2,097 of 4,727 Fall 2025 transfer applicants), but that headline is a blend. Binghamton lists no single GPA floor — CDS D6/D7 both say 'Varies by School.' The realistic admit is a SUNY community college student with 24+ credits and roughly a 3.3-3.5 who applied to Harpur College of Arts and Sciences; Watson (engineering/CS) and the School of Management run well below the university rate and expect completed prerequisite sequences. College transcript and a statement of good standing are required of all; standardized tests are not required for transfers.
levers: SUNY seamless transfer: finish the SUNY Transfer Path courses for your major plus an A.A./A.S. at a SUNY community college to arrive with SUNY general education met and junior standing — the single biggest structural advantage a NY community college applicant has here.

Pick the entry school deliberately. Harpur College is the widest door; School of Management and Watson admit against capacity and prerequisites, and moving into them after you enroll is not guaranteed — so apply directly to the school you want, with its prereqs already done.
watchouts: Watson College (especially CS) and the School of Management are the capacity-constrained programs; a GPA that clears Harpur will not clear them, and internal transfer into them post-enrollment is competitive, not automatic.

Credit cap: CDS D13/D14 cap transferred credit at 82 credits (all external credit included) and the lowest transferable grade is C-, so extra community college credits past the cap and any C-minus-or-below coursework will not carry.
feeders: Overwhelmingly SUNY community colleges — SUNY Broome (adjacent, and the Binghamton Advantage Program partner that routes students onto campus), plus downstate feeders like Suffolk County CC, Nassau CC, Westchester CC, Rockland CC and Monroe CC; some lateral mo

name: Boston College
typical: BC admits roughly a quarter of transfer applicants — typically strong B+/A- records in traditional liberal-arts coursework, many from Jesuit/Catholic and other four-year colleges; 9+ credits required to apply as a transfer.
levers: Spring entry (Nov 1) is a real second window with a smaller pool
Mirror BC's core — philosophy/theology-friendly coursework signals Morrissey fit better than a purely preprofessional transcript
watchouts: Connell Nursing and Carroll (business) take very few transfers — most seats are Morrissey Arts & Sciences
Housing is not guaranteed for transfer students

name: Boston University
typical: One of the largest transfer operations in the country — 2,416 admits, 840 enrolled. You need 12+ credits and must declare a specific school/major; accepted transfers average around a 3.7-3.8, and CC students with strong records transfer in regularly.
levers: Volume is the lever: a 35.7% transfer rate is roughly 3x BU's first-year rate
Spring entry (Nov 1) plus up to 68 accepted credits keeps most applicants on schedule
watchouts: College-specific prerequisites gate Questrom, ENG, and Sargent
Transfer merit aid is scarce and packages run weaker than first-year offers

name: Brandeis
cycle: 2024-2025 CDS (Fall 2024 entering) — the 2025-26 CDS is posted but its URL returned 403 at research time, so these are prior-year figures
typical: 581 applied, 287 admitted, 81 enrolled for Fall 2024 (CDS D2: men 269/114/34, women 312/173/47). Brandeis admits roughly 3.5 transfers for every one who enrolls, which is why the rate sits near half — this is one of the genuinely accessible transfer doors among selective private research universities. The admitted student is typically one to two years into another four-year or a community college with solid college grades; the college transcript and essay do the work, and Brandeis lists a statement of good standing from prior institutions among its required items (CDS D5).
levers: Spring entry is a real second cycle, not a formality: CDS D9 lists a November 1 spring closing date with notification around December 5, against a fraction of fall's 581 applications. Same application, same requirements, materially thinner pool.

Only 12 completed college credits are needed to be read as a transfer rather than a first-year applicant (CDS D4) — a single full semester elsewhere qualifies you, so a student unhappy after one term at another school can move for sophomore fall instead of waiting a year.
watchouts: 64-credit cap from both two-year and four-year schools (CDS D13/D14) and 64 credits must be completed at Brandeis for the bachelor's (D16). A completed associate degree covers exactly half the degree and no more — plan on two full years at Brandeis no matter how many credits you bring.

The Brandeis Core still applies to transfers — writing, foreign language proficiency, and the experiential-learning requirement — and clearing all three inside four semesters alongside a major is the usual reason a transfer needs a fifth semester. Sort the language requirement before you arrive.
feeders: Not reported in the CDS. In practice: Massachusetts and greater-Boston community colleges, other New England four-years, and lateral moves from larger public flagships. Note that Brandeis is private and therefore outside MassTransfer, which covers Massachusetts public institutions only — there is no state guarantee or automatic articulation into Brandeis, so every credit is evaluated individually.

name: Buffalo
typical: CDS D2 for Fall 2025: 4,663 transfer applicants, 3,052 admitted, 1,493 enrolled — a 65.5% transfer admit rate, far more forgiving than UB's first-year rate. The stated floor is a 2.5 college GPA with at least 12 semester hours completed (CDS D4/D7). The modal admit is a SUNY community college student arriving with an AA/AS finished and entering at junior standing. UB's own CDS adds that 'entry at junior level requires higher GPA for some programs,' so the 65% headline number masks the competitive majors underneath it.
levers: SUNY seamless transfer: an AA/AS from a SUNY two-year carries junior standing and completed SUNY general education. Before you register for any semester, run each course through UB's TAURUS articulation tool (buffalo.edu/taurus.html, the articulation link UB names in its own CDS) so you only take courses that land as major or gen-ed credit.

Credit-friendly policies you can plan around: UB reports no maximum on credits transferable from either two-year or four-year institutions, accepts a D- as the lowest transferable grade, and requires only 30 credits earned at UB for the bachelor's (CDS D12-D16). Loading up cheap community college credits genuinely pays off here.
watchouts: Admission to UB is not admission to the major. Engineering and computer science (SEAS) and the School of Management run their own, tougher transfer screens with specific prerequisite sequences, and UB's CDS states plainly that junior-level entry requires a higher GPA for some programs.

Apply with fewer than 24 credits and your high school transcript plus SAT/ACT scores come back into the review (CDS D11) — the profile you were trying to leave behind. Cross 24 credits first if your high school record is weak.
feeders: Predominantly Western New York SUNY two-years — SUNY Erie, Monroe CC, Genesee CC, Niagara County CC — plus downstate feeders like Nassau CC and Suffolk County CC, and lateral transfers from other SUNY four-year campuses.

name: CSU Northridge
typical: A completion test more than a selection contest: 10,027 of 13,924 transfer applicants admitted (72.0%). The profile that gets in is a California community college student with 60+ transferable semester units, the Golden Four done with C- or better (CSUN requires at least English composition and math), and a 2.0+ transferable GPA in a non-impacted major. Only 4,335 of 10,027 admits enrolled (43% yield), so CSUN admits deep into its pool. IMPORTANT SOURCING NOTE: CSUN files this PDF under '2025-2026' on its Institutional Research page, but the document's own running header reads 'Common Data Set 2024-2025' on 47 of 48 pages and D2 explicitly asks for students enrolled in Fall 2024 — so these are Fall 2024 entrants, not Fall 2025. Numbers verified from the D2 table directly (Men 6,395/4,579/1,997; Women 7,470/5,406/2,317; Another Gender 59/42/21).
levers: Earn an AA-T/AS-T (ADT) in a similar major: CSU-guaranteed admission with junior standing. CSUN publishes an ADT-to-major map showing which community college ADTs land in which CSUN degree, so verify your specific pairing on ASSIST before you finish the degree.

Declare a non-impacted major. Only Cinema and Television Arts (Film and TV Production options, 2.10 GPA) and Music (audition) are impacted for Fall 2026/Spring 2027 — everything else admits at the 2.0 CSU floor. Major choice is the single biggest admissions lever at this campus.
watchouts: Local/regional-area impaction is no longer in effect at CSUN, so older advice about needing a San Fernando Valley address for preference is stale — do not pay for strategy built on it.

At 60+ semester units you must declare a real major and can no longer apply as 'Undecided.' A late switch into Cinema/TV or Music also means an earlier deadline (Jan 31 and Jan 15) and can cost a full cycle.
feeders: Draws primarily from the Los Angeles and San Fernando Valley community college network — Los Angeles Valley College, Pierce College, LA Mission College, Glendale Community College, Santa Monica College, College of the Canyons, and Moorpark College. Regional dr

name: Cal Poly SLO
typical: Junior-level transfers only — Cal Poly considers applicants who will have 90 quarter / 60 semester transferable units by entry, and does not admit lower-division transfers. Admitted students have finished essentially every course on their major's published required-course list and carry GPAs far above the 2.0 minimum the CDS reports, typically clustering in the 3.5-4.0 range. Cal Poly runs each application through a major-specific selection formula that scores GPA plus completion of the named required courses, so the 21.2% overall rate masks enormous spread: engineering, business and computer science run far below it, while less-subscribed majors run above.
levers: Complete every course on your major's Cal Poly transfer selection guide before entry, and list each one in the correct section of the Cal State Apply application. Cal Poly scores applications through admission-selection software built for each specific major, and you only receive points for required courses you actually report — an unreported completed course scores the same as a course you never took.

Choose the major deliberately. Cal Poly admits by major, publishes which majors are open to transfer applicants each cycle, and does not consider an alternate major — applying to a closed or heavily oversubscribed program is an outright loss rather than a redirect. Shifting to an open, lower-demand major within the same college is the single largest movement you can make on your odds.
watchouts: The ADT does not get you into Cal Poly. An AA-T/AS-T in a similar major guarantees admission with junior standing somewhere in the CSU system and earns priority consideration, but Cal Poly is impacted in every major, so that systemwide guarantee is routinely honored by redirecting you to a different campus. Treat the ADT as the eligibility floor, not the ticket.

Fall-only entry with a hard Nov 30 close — CDS D9 lists dates for fall alone (closing 11/30, notification 4/1, reply 5/1) and leaves winter, spring and summer blank. Cal Poly also converted from quarters to semesters in Fall 2026, so ASSIST agreements and transfer selection guides written in quarter units need to be re-verified against the current lists before you lock in a course plan.
feeders: Cuesta College, Cal Poly's local San Luis Obispo County college, plus the high-volume Central Coast and statewide CCCs — Allan Hancock, Santa Barbara City, Moorpark, De Anza, Diablo Valley, Pasadena City, Santa Monica and Orange Coast. There is no UC-style TAG at Cal Poly, so the pattern is statewide rather than partner-based: admits come from students anywhere in California who followed a published transfer selection guide course-for-course.

name: Cal State Fullerton
typical: A California community college student who has completed 60 transferable semester units and the CSU "Golden Four" (oral communication, written communication, critical thinking, college math) with at least a 2.0 — most often holding an ADT from an Orange County or LA-area community college. The 77.1% headline is real but misleading as a personal odds estimate: CSUF is impacted campus-wide, so admission is decided major-by-major, and an ADT holder in a similar major with local-area status is admitted near-automatically while a non-local applicant to Nursing or a Mihaylo business concentration can be denied at a GPA well above 3.0. Of 17,127 admits only 5,061 enrolled, so the admit pool is far wider than the class.
levers: Finish an ADT (AA-T/AS-T) in a major CSUF designates "similar" to your intended major. This is the single largest lever: it guarantees CSU-system admission with junior standing, caps the remaining degree at 60 units, and drops you into the ADT pool that is evaluated ahead of non-ADT applicants for the same impacted major. Confirm the similar-major designation on the CSU ADT/ADT-similar list before your last CC term — an ADT in a major CSUF does not treat as similar loses the priority.

Claim local admission area status. Because every CSUF major is impacted, the campus applies supplementary admission criteria with a lower GPA threshold for applicants from its designated local service area (the North Orange County Community College District — Fullerton College and Cypress College — plus local-area high schools). Same major, same GPA, different outcome depending on which side of the local line you applied from.
watchouts: The ADT guarantee runs to the CSU system, not to Fullerton. If CSUF cannot accommodate you in an impacted major, you are redirected to another CSU campus with space — so applying only to CSUF on the strength of an ADT can land you at a campus you never picked. Apply to a second and third CSU.

Every major is impacted and each carries its own GPA cutoff far above the 2.0 CSU floor — historically Nursing, the Mihaylo business concentrations, Computer Science, Engineering, and Kinesiology are the tightest. "CSU-admissible" is not "CSUF-major-admissible." All coursework, including the ADT itself, must be complete by the end of the spring term before fall entry; an in-progress ADT at the deadline does not count.
feeders: Overwhelmingly Orange County and Los Angeles-area California community colleges. Its own local district — Fullerton College and Cypress College (North Orange County CCD) — supplies the largest and most-favored share, followed by Santa Ana College, Orange Coast College, Santiago Canyon, Golden West, Saddleback, Irvine Valley, Mt. SAC, Long Beach City, Pasadena City, and Riverside City. Very little out-of-state or four-year-to-four-year volume; this is a regional CCC-to-CSU pipeline.

name: Cal State Long Beach
typical: Upper-division transfers from Southern California community colleges with 60 transferable semester units, the Golden Four done with C or better, 30 units of GE, and good standing at the prior institution. The published minimum GPA is 2.00, but that number almost never decides the case: CSULB ranks applicants on major-specific degree requirements (MSDR), so admission turns on whether the exact lower-division prep courses for that major are complete. Roughly one in two applicants is admitted overall, with impacted and highly impacted majors far tighter.
levers: Secure local preference (Long Beach College Promise). Local status is determined by high school of graduation in CSULB's local area, or by military veteran status. For all majors except 'Highly Impacted' ones, CSU-eligible local applicants are admitted outright if they meet the major's minimum cumulative GPA and lower-division prep; for highly impacted majors, local preference adds 0.1 to the GPA used in competitive ranking.

Complete an ADT in a similar major: it guarantees CSU admission with junior standing and 60 units of credit, which protects against credit loss and locks in upper-division status. Confirm the ADT maps to CSULB's MSDR list for the specific major, since the ADT guarantee does not exempt you from highly impacted major ranking.
watchouts: Highly Impacted majors layer supplemental criteria on top of the application (interviews, auditions, portfolios, or extra academic credentials) and require a separate supplemental application; ranking is by MSDR completion plus that supplemental review.

Major-Specific Degree Requirements are pass/fail gatekeepers published per college and per cycle. One missing prep course can remove a 3.8 GPA applicant from the pool, and the Fall 2026 MSDR lists differ from Fall 2025.
feeders: Predominantly Southern California community colleges. Long Beach City College is the formal partner through the Long Beach College Promise, which is the structured LBCC-to-CSULB pipeline; the surrounding Los Angeles and Orange County colleges supply most of the remaining volume. Local preference, though, is keyed to high school of graduation rather than which community college you attended.

name: Cal State San Marcos
typical: About five of every six transfer applicants are admitted, so for a non-impacted major the decision is closer to a checklist than a competition: 60+ transferable semester units, a 2.0+ transferable GPA (CA residents), and the Golden Four — written communication, oral communication, critical thinking, and college-level math — completed with C- or better by the spring before entry. ADT holders clear this comfortably. The 83% is diluted by that open-door posture and does not describe Business Administration or the Traditional BSN, which are screened separately.
levers: Earn an AA-T/AS-T in a similar major: it carries the statewide CSU guarantee, gets you priority consideration at CSUSM, and caps you at roughly 60 more units to the degree.

Finish the Golden Four with C- or better before the application-year spring term — CSUSM verifies these against your Feb 15 transcripts, and an incomplete Golden Four is the most common reason an otherwise-admissible file is denied.
watchouts: Two transfer majors are impacted and the 83% does not apply to them: Business Administration screens on a competitive pre-business core GPA, and the Traditional BSN rank-orders applicants on published supplemental criteria.
The application closes Dec 1 but official transcripts are due Feb 15 — late or missing transcripts, not the application itself, are what usually sink admissible files.
feeders: CSUSM's own local-area list names Palomar College, MiraCosta College, Mt. San Jacinto College, and Imperial Valley College (cited explicitly for TBSN local priority). North County San Diego community colleges are the core pipeline; CSUSM does not publish a ran

name: Caltech
typical: A literal handful: 11 of 178 admitted, 10 enrolled — some years fewer. Admits enter as sophomores or juniors after Caltech's five transfer entrance exams (calc, linear algebra, mechanics, E&M/statistical physics, special relativity) with coursework mirroring the core.
levers: Train specifically for the five entrance exams — they are the gate; straight-A transcripts don't substitute
Shape your schedule to Caltech's core (math through linear algebra, calc-based physics through special relativity) before applying
watchouts: Single-digit admits most years — treat it as a lottery layered on a solid plan, never the plan
No senior-year entry, no bachelor's holders, and credit standing is assessed only after admission

name: Case Western
typical: A genuinely selective transfer path at 26.2%, far tighter than most private-university transfer doors and not much softer than CWRU's first-year rate. Only 51 of 173 admits enrolled (about 29% yield), so a large share of admits treat CWRU as a backup and aid is often the deciding factor. Admitted transfers are typically STEM- and pre-health-oriented students with strong college GPAs, applying with C-or-better transferable coursework; high school transcript, college transcripts, essay, and a statement of good standing are all required.
levers: Be an active Phi Theta Kappa member — CWRU awards a $25,000-per-year PTK scholarship to admitted transfers, and all transfers get automatic merit-scholarship consideration. At a high-sticker private with a 29% transfer yield, the money lever is the admission lever.

Use the 3/2 Engineering dual-degree route from a partner liberal-arts college: apply by Feb 15 with 90 semester hours (135 quarter hours), a 3.00 overall GPA and a 3.00 in math and science. It is a defined-criteria pathway with a separate, earlier calendar and March 1 notification rather than open competitive review.
watchouts: The published deadlines conflict with the CDS: CDS D9 lists a fall closing date of 6/1 (priority 5/15, notification 7/1), while the admission site lists an Early Plan of March 15 (notification from April 1) and a Regular Plan of July 1. Confirm directly with admissions — applying on the late end compresses aid and housing.

CWRU requires 60 credits completed in residence for the bachelor's (CDS D16) and transfers only C-or-better coursework (CDS D12), so a completed associate degree will not reliably clear half the degree in every major, particularly in engineering and nursing sequences.
feeders: Not disclosed by CWRU — the CDS does not break out sending institutions. Structurally the pipeline is Northeast Ohio community colleges, four-year transfers into STEM and pre-health programs, and 3/2 engineering partner liberal-arts colleges, but specific feeder campuses are not published and should not be represented as verified.

name: Clemson
typical: The 58% headline masks a bimodal pool: Bridge to Clemson students who cleared 30 credits at 2.5 transition in almost automatically, while outside applicants to capacity-limited majors face a far harder screen. The typical admit has 30+ transferable semester hours, a college GPA of 2.5 minimum (well above that for engineering, business and nursing), freshman-level Math, Science and English finished, and every transferred course graded C or higher.
levers: Bridge to Clemson, the invitation-only year at Tri-County Technical College where you live on Clemson's campus: finish 30 transferable credits at a 2.5 GPA with all courses graded C or higher and you move into Clemson as a sophomore. The invitation comes off the freshman application, so this lever has to be pulled a year before you would otherwise transfer.

Apply on the SC TRAC statewide transfer block with 30+ transferable hours already banked, and clear freshman Math, Science and English before you apply. Clemson's own CDS names that coursework as an expectation, so it functions as a screen rather than a suggestion, and beating the 2.5 floor by a wide margin is what carries a competitive major.
watchouts: Clemson's CDS states outright that not all majors are open to transfer applicants. Engineering, nursing and other capacity-limited programs gate separately, so a 2.5 overall does not buy you into an impacted major.
37 of your last 43 hours must be completed in residence at Clemson, and the lowest grade that transfers is a C. Credits picked up elsewhere late in the game will not count toward the degree.
feeders: Tri-County Technical College dominates by a wide margin through the Bridge program, followed by Greenville Technical College, Trident Technical College, Midlands Technical College and Spartanburg Community College. Secondary flow comes from four-year swirl wit

name: Colorado Boulder
cycle: Fall 2024 entry (CDS 2025-2026 — CU Boulder's newest CDS reports Fall 2024 in D2)
typical: Roughly seven in ten transfer applicants are admitted, but residency splits the class sharply: CU Boulder's own D2 residency table shows in-state applicants admitted at 84% (1,390 of 1,645) versus 65% out-of-state (1,848 of 2,827). There is no minimum credit threshold (D4 = No), and minimum GPA varies by college rather than being set university-wide (D6/D7), so the binding constraint is the target college's prerequisites, not a universal cutoff.
levers: Come through a Colorado community college: complete an Associate of Arts or Science with Designation (DwD), which by Colorado statute guarantees junior standing and transfer of the full 60 credits to CU Boulder.
Finish the 31-credit gtPathways general-education block before transferring — it transfers course-for-course to every Colorado public institution and locks in the 84% in-state admit lane.
watchouts: CU Boulder requires a high school transcript from every transfer applicant (CDS D5), which catches applicants who assume their college record is all that matters; Engineering and Leeds also set prerequisite and GPA bars above the 72% headline.
The College of Music requires a separate College of Music application, a letter of reference, and a scheduled audition on top of the admission application (CDS D8).
feeders: Front Range Community College, Community College of Denver, Arapahoe Community College, and Pikes Peak State College anchor the in-state pipeline. Out-of-state applicants actually outnumber in-state (2,827 vs 1,645) but are admitted at a far lower rate and enr

name: Colorado State
cycle: Fall 2025 entering class (CDS FY2026, published March 2026)
typical: About two of every three transfer applicants are admitted (2,794 of 4,292), and 1,567 of those admits enrolled — 1,325 full-time, 242 part-time. The realistic admit is a Colorado community college student who is finishing or has finished an AA/AS and is carrying roughly a 3.0. Two policies CSU states directly shape who succeeds: the lowest grade it will accept for transfer credit is a C-, and it takes at most 64 semester credits from a two-year institution. Admission is to a major, not just to the university, so the 65% headline is a university-wide average, not the bar for your program.
levers: Colorado's statewide Degree with Designation (the AA/AS with Designation) is the strongest lever: finish the matching associate degree at a Colorado public two-year college and you transfer into CSU with junior standing and your lower-division major requirements treated as satisfied. Confirm your intended major actually has a Degree with Designation pathway before you build the plan around it.

GT Pathways, Colorado's guaranteed-transfer general education course set, moves gen ed credit from any Colorado public institution to CSU without re-taking anything — load GT-coded sections deliberately. Pair that with CSU's rolling review: the fall priority date is February 1 even though the file does not close until July 31, and spring entry has its own November 1 priority date if a fall seat is tight.
watchouts: The 64-semester-credit cap from two-year schools is a hard ceiling. Credits banked past 64 at a community college do not carry, so finishing the associate degree and moving beats stockpiling extra terms.

Admission is to the major. Engineering, computer science, and business set their own standards above the university floor, so check the specific program's requirement rather than planning against the 65% overall rate — and note the C- minimum means a D in a prerequisite has to be retaken.
feeders: Front Range Community College (Larimer, Westminster, and Boulder County campuses) is the dominant feeder given proximity to Fort Collins, followed by Aims Community College in Greeley, Arapahoe Community College, Community College of Denver, Red Rocks Communit

name: Delaware
cycle: Fall 2024 (CDS 2024-25; UD's 2025-26 CDS was not posted at time of check)
typical: UD admitted 1,157 of 2,033 transfer applicants (56.9%) and enrolled 642. The admitted pool leans heavily on Delaware Tech students in Connected Degree pathways and on UD's own Associate in Arts Program students continuing to Newark, usually with a full year of credit and a GPA near 3.0 — well above the 2.0 CDS floor, which UD annotates as 'Some majors require a higher GPA or coursework.'
levers: Delaware Tech Connected Degree: complete the designated associate degree in a Connected Degree pathway and you move into the matching UD bachelor's program on completion of the GPA and course requirements — the same structure exists with Cecil, Harford, Brookdale, and Rowan College at Gloucester County.
Start in UD's own Associate in Arts Program (Dover, Georgetown, Wilmington), finish the AA, and continue to the Newark campus as a UD student rather than competing in the external transfer pool.
watchouts: Nursing is not open to transfer applicants at all, and Engineering, business, and computer science run far above the 2.0 CDS minimum — published major minimums reach 3.45.

Fall review is rolling from January, so the June 1 date is a suggestion, not a cutoff; seats in the selective majors are gone long before it. Also plan for residency: 30 of your final 36 credits must be earned at UD.
feeders: Delaware Tech campuses via Connected Degree and UD's own Associate in Arts Program sites, plus nearby out-of-state two-years — Cecil and Harford (MD), Brookdale and Rowan College at Gloucester County (NJ).

name: Drexel
typical: CDS D2 shows 2,596 transfer applicants, 1,511 admitted, 499 enrolled - a 33% yield, so most admits go elsewhere. Drexel's own floor (CDS D7) is a 2.5 college GPA; the students who actually land here cluster nearer 3.0-3.5 with 30+ completed credits, and come as often from other four-years as from community colleges. Drexel runs on quarters and admits transfers in all four terms (D3) on rolling review, so the pool is spread across the year rather than bunched at one fall deadline. Note the split: 991 men applied vs 1,557 women, and men were admitted at 63.6% vs 54.6% for women - a real gap driven by major mix (engineering vs health professions).
levers: Dual-admission / transfer partnership agreements with the Philadelphia-area two-years (Community College of Philadelphia, Montgomery County CC, Delaware County CC, Bucks County CC, Camden County College). These carry guaranteed-admission language and partnership scholarship money, but you have to enroll in the agreement at the community college - signing it in your final term forfeits most of the benefit.

Off-cycle entry. CDS D3 confirms Drexel admits transfers for Fall, Winter, Spring AND Summer, all rolling (D9). Winter and spring quarter starts are a genuinely thinner door than fall, and because review is rolling, an application submitted months before the April 15 fall priority date is read against an emptier class than one submitted on it.
watchouts: The quarter system is a credit-loss trap. Semester credits convert at 1.5 quarter credits each, and CDS D13/D14 cap transfer credit at 60 credits from a two-year AND 60 from a four-year. A completed associate degree does not automatically buy junior standing, and the co-op sequence frequently pushes transfers onto a five-year plan.

The 58.2% university-wide rate badly overstates your odds in the direct-entry health programs. Nursing (ACE), Physician Assistant and the accelerated BS/MD-type programs run separate, far more restrictive transfer processes - some accept no external transfers at all.
feeders: Philadelphia-metro two-years dominate: Community College of Philadelphia, Montgomery County CC, Delaware County CC, Bucks County CC, and Camden County College (NJ). Meaningful four-year lateral flow as well - Penn State branch campuses, Temple, and Rowan - whi

name: Florida
typical: The overwhelming majority are Florida College System students finishing an A.A. degree under the state's 2+2 articulation guarantee, arriving with junior standing and the major's Common Prerequisite Manual courses already done. Roughly 2,124 of the 2,633 admits actually enrolled, a yield near 81%, which is the signature of an in-state pipeline rather than a national applicant pool.
levers: Earn the Florida A.A. at a Florida College System institution: state 2+2 articulation guarantees admission to a State University System school with junior standing and general education certified, and UF gives admission preference to A.A. holders over credit-only transfers.

Enroll in Gator Engineering at Santa Fe College, the co-located 2+2 that lets you take UF engineering coursework in Gainesville and continue into the Herbert Wertheim College of Engineering; UF Online and PaCE students likewise have a defined on-campus transition path after 60 credits.
watchouts: The 44.9% headline is a campus-wide average and hides limited-access programs. Nursing, Warrington business, and engineering screen on major-specific prerequisite GPA through a separate departmental review, so your real odds are the major's, not the university's.
CDS D13 caps transferable credit from a two-year institution at 60 semester credits, so anything you bank past an A.A. at a community college is unlikely to count toward the degree.
feeders: Florida College System campuses dominate: Santa Fe College (adjacent to UF), Valencia, Miami Dade, Broward, Hillsborough CC, St. Petersburg College. UF's own UF Online and PaCE students form a large internal feeder. Out-of-state and four-year lateral transfers are a small minority.

name: Fordham
cycle: 2019-2020 CDS (Fall 2019 entering) — the most recent Common Data Set Fordham has published publicly; no 2020-21 through 2024-25 CDS exists on its site
typical: CDS D2 for Fall 2019: 1,463 transfer applicants, 730 admitted, 323 enrolled — a 49.9% admit rate on a self-selected pool. That same CDS lists a required minimum college GPA of 3.00, so the realistic admit has completed at least a year of full-time college work with a 3.0+ and applies into one of three undergraduate colleges (Fordham College at Rose Hill, Fordham College at Lincoln Center, or the Gabelli School of Business). Fordham requires a high school diploma or equivalency, transcripts from every institution attended, an essay, and a Mid-Term Report if you have under 24 post-high-school credits. Treat the 49.9% as a stale baseline, not current-year odds.
levers: Apply early inside the rolling window, not at the deadline: Fordham's fall transfer application opens November 1 and closes June 1, but decisions are released on a rolling basis beginning March 15. A complete file in March or April competes for a fuller set of seats than a June 1 submission.

Choose the college and campus deliberately, and use spring as a genuine second door. You apply to exactly one of Fordham College at Rose Hill, Fordham College at Lincoln Center, or Gabelli (at Rose Hill or Lincoln Center) with a matching major. Spring entry has its own cycle (opens August 1, closes November 1, decisions rolling from October 24), and Gabelli explicitly accepts both fall and spring transfers.
watchouts: The 60-credit ceiling redirects you to a different school. Fordham accepts a maximum of 60 transfer credit hours into its three traditional undergraduate colleges and requires at least two years of full-time coursework in residence (the 2019-20 CDS lists 64 credits minimum to earn the bachelor's at Fordham). Students who arrive with more than 60 credits are steered to the School of Professional and Continuing Studies (PCS) instead — a near-complete associate-plus student can be admitted to a different school than the one they pictured. Courses also need 3+ credit hours and a grade of C or better to transfer at all.

The admit rate is six years old. Fordham stopped publishing its CDS after 2019-2020, so there is no verifiable recent transfer rate. Anyone quoting a current Fordham transfer percentage is not sourcing it from Fordham's own CDS.
feeders: Heavily New York metro. The transfer pipeline runs from CUNY and SUNY two-year campuses (Borough of Manhattan CC, Bronx CC, Westchester CC and peers) plus regional four-year schools, with New York students who commute to Rose Hill or Lincoln Center. Two markers confirm the pattern: Fordham waives the $80 application fee for community college students in Phi Theta Kappa, and it runs a dedicated pathway for students currently in New York's HEOP/EOP/CD/SEEK opportunity programs, answered through the Common App Member Questions for transfers.

name: GWU
typical: Verified D2: 2,229 applied, 1,339 admitted, 582 enrolled (43.5% yield). Transfer admission is dramatically softer than GW's first-year round — roughly three in five get in. GW sets no minimum college GPA and no minimum credit count (CDS D4 = No), so you can apply after a single college course; most admits enter as sophomores or juniors. Required: college transcripts, high school transcript, essay, and a statement of good standing from every prior institution. Interview not required; test scores recommended of some only. Minimum grade of C- for a course to carry credit.
levers: GW's School of Medicine and Health Sciences runs named guaranteed-admission agreements with partner community colleges: an earned AA, AS, or AAS routes you directly into the BS in Health Sciences or the dual-degree option — the only true guarantee GW publishes.
Use spring or summer entry. GW admits transfers in all three terms and the spring window (Aug 15-Oct 1, decisions by early December) draws a far smaller pool than the ~2,229-applicant fall round.
watchouts: GW requires a minimum 60 credits earned in residence at GW for the bachelor's, so credits past roughly 60 buy you nothing — arriving with 90 still leaves two full years and two years of tuition.

Corcoran BFA majors require a portfolio review (all except Interior Architecture), and transfer aid is need-based only with no published merit award — file the aid application by the admissions deadline or you are competing for nothing.
feeders: No official feeder breakdown is published by GW. The documented pipelines are the DMV two-year colleges — Montgomery College posts course-by-course GW articulation pathways indexed by catalog year, and Northern Virginia Community College lists GW among its tra

name: Georgia
typical: In-state students coming from a Georgia public two-year or state college with at least 30 transferable hours and a GPA above UGA's published consideration line for their credit band (3.50+ at 30-59 hours, 3.20+ at 60+ hours for Fall 2026), typically with the USG general-education core well underway. Out-of-state transfers are a thin slice of the 1,893 who enrolled.
levers: Cross 60 transferable semester hours before you apply: UGA's Fall 2026 consideration line drops from 3.50 (30-59 hours) to 3.20 (60+ hours), and the secondary-review band drops from 3.30-3.49 to 3.00-3.19.

Complete the University System of Georgia's Core IMPACTS general-education core at a Georgia public institution — it transfers as a block across USG, and for Terry College it lets you arrive with the business prerequisites finished, since the internal major application is a separate hurdle (2.6+ overall GPA minimum).
watchouts: Under 30 transferable hours UGA reads you as a first-year applicant, not a transfer (CDS D4 sets the minimum at 30 credits) — and D6 shows a 3.00 high school GPA floor still applies to some transfer applicants.

Admission to UGA is not admission to Terry College of Business: no one is admitted directly into a business major from outside the university, everyone enters as 'intended business,' and UGA restates the transfer GPA thresholds each term based on space.
feeders: Overwhelmingly in-state Georgia public two-year and state colleges — Georgia State's Perimeter College campuses, Georgia Gwinnett, Georgia Highlands, Athens Technical and Gwinnett Technical — plus laterals from Kennesaw State and Georgia Southern. Out-of-state

name: Georgia Tech
typical: Transfers need 30+ semester hours, two English comps, and the major-specific math/lab-science chart, with GPA floors of 3.3 (Computing/Engineering) and 3.0 elsewhere — but floors are eligibility, not admission: real admits run well above and skew toward pathway invitees and Georgia residents.
levers: Pathway programs are the widest door: Arts & Sciences, Conditional, First-Generation, Talent Initiative, and Veterans pathways give denied first-years a defined route after a year elsewhere
Regents' Engineering Pathway (REPP) and Dual Degree Engineering start you at a partner Georgia school and finish in the College of Engineering
watchouts: Unaffiliated out-of-state applicants face much steeper odds than the 20% headline
Meeting the 3.3/3.0 floor only makes you eligible — competitive Computing admits run substantially higher
feeders: Georgia pathway partners and in-state colleges

name: Howard
typical: A floor-clearing admit, not a lottery. Howard admitted 701 of 910 transfer applicants for Fall 2024 (77.0%) and enrolled 190 — a 27% yield, which is why the rate runs high: Howard admits broadly and loses most admits to other offers. The published bar is concrete: 15+ transferable credit hours from a regionally accredited institution, a 2.5 cumulative college GPA, and C or better in college-level English and Math. CDS D5 marks the high school transcript, interview, and standardized test scores as NOT required of transfers, so your college record and those two gateway courses carry the file almost entirely. The exception is the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, where portfolios (Art, Architecture & Design) and auditions (Theatre, Music) gate the major rather than the university. Applicant pool skews heavily female: 612 women vs 297 men applied.
levers: Clear the published floor exactly and visibly: 15+ transferable credits, 2.5 cumulative GPA, and a C or better in college-level English AND college-level Math. Those two gateway courses are named explicitly by Howard and are the most common reason an otherwise fine file stalls — take them before you apply, not concurrently. The single required recommendation must come from a professor or academic advisor, not a work supervisor.

Check your current college against Howard's registrar transfer-credit and articulation-agreements page (howard.edu/registrar/transfer-credit-articulation-agreements, the URL Howard itself cites in CDS D22) BEFORE you register for another term. Howard caps transfer credit at 60 hours and requires a C minimum (CDS D12), so courses graded C- or below are dead weight no matter how well they map.
watchouts: The 60-credit cap applies to both two-year and four-year sources (CDS D13/D14), and 30 credits minimum must be earned at Howard for the bachelor's (D16). A completed associate degree does not guarantee junior standing — verify course-by-course before assuming a two-year finish.

Howard's CDS D9 fall/spring deadline rows are swapped: the Fall row lists Nov 1 priority / Nov 15 closing, which are actually the spring dates. Howard's admission site is the reliable source — April 1 for fall, November 1 for spring.
feeders: Howard publishes no transfer feeder list, and none appears in the CDS. The only official source naming partner institutions is the registrar's transfer-credit and articulation-agreements page, which Howard cites itself in CDS D22. The volume argues against a n

name: Illinois
typical: CDS D2 for Fall 2024: 5,715 transfer applicants, 2,748 admitted, 1,547 enrolled. Illinois reports no minimum college GPA in D7 and answers D8/D11 with "Requirements vary by program" because each college sets its own bar - competitive admits generally hold roughly 3.0-3.5+ with the target major's specific prerequisite sequence already completed. Illinois community college students following an IAI or Pathway agreement make up the bulk of admits. Note D4: Illinois sets no minimum credit count to apply as a transfer, so applicants with under a year of college compete here rather than in the first-year pool.
levers: Engineering Pathways: a guaranteed-admission agreement into The Grainger College of Engineering from partner Illinois community colleges (College of DuPage, Parkland, Oakton, Harper and others). Complete the named course sequence and GPA requirements and admission to Grainger is guaranteed - but Chemical Engineering and the CS+X majors (except Bioengineering and Physics) are administered outside Grainger and are NOT covered by the guarantee.

Parkland Pathway to Illinois: dual enrollment at Parkland College and UIUC, requiring full-time status (12+ hours combined) each fall and spring, each-semester meetings with both Parkland and Illinois advisors, and meeting the intended major's transfer requirements from the Transfer Handbook. Engineering applicants must take the proctored ALEKS math assessment at Parkland and score at least 76 to complete the application by the April 5 deadline. Pair either pathway with the Illinois Articulation Initiative General Education Core Curriculum (GECC), which transfers as a block and satisfies Illinois general education.
watchouts: You are admitted to a college and major, not to the university, and the 48.1% overall rate averages away the real gates - Grainger Engineering (Computer Science especially) and Gies Business run dramatically tighter than the headline. Illinois's own CDS answers both D8 and D11 with "Requirements vary by program," so check the Transfer Handbook entry for the exact major before assuming the aggregate number applies.

Illinois requires a high school transcript AND an essay or personal statement of ALL transfer applicants (CDS D501/D503), which trips up applicants who assume college coursework alone carries the file. Separately, D1601 requires 45 credits completed at Illinois for the bachelor's degree, so even a heavily credited transfer owes more than two full semesters on campus. Illinois also grants ACE military credit but does not accept CLEP or DSST (D1802/D1803).
feeders: Illinois community colleges moving through the Illinois Articulation Initiative and formal pathway agreements - Parkland College in Champaign (via Parkland Pathway to Illinois) is the signature feeder, with College of DuPage, Harper College, Oakton, and Heartland prominent through Engineering Pathways and IAI GECC transfer. A meaningful secondary flow comes from other Illinois four-year institutions and from intra-university transfers between UIUC colleges.

name: Indiana
typical: About five of every eight transfer applicants are admitted (1,326 of 2,119). The published floors are just 12 completed semester hours (D4) and a 2.50 college GPA (D7), but realistic admits sit meaningfully above that and have cleared gen-ed through Indiana's statewide transfer core; Ivy Tech and Vincennes students holding a completed transfer associate are the most reliable admits.
levers: Complete the Indiana Statewide Transfer General Education Core (STGEC) — the 30-credit block transfers to IU as a whole and satisfies most gen-ed, which is the main defense against credit loss.
Use a TSAP (Transfer Single Articulation Pathway) associate degree from Ivy Tech or Vincennes — Indiana statute guarantees the full 60 credits and junior standing at IU Bloomington.
watchouts: Admission to IU is not admission to Kelley — the business school runs its own standard-admission review with separate GPA and prerequisite coursework, far tougher than the 62.6% headline.
Jacobs School of Music requires a supplemental application and, in some cases, an audition (CDS D8), on a separate timeline from the university application.
feeders: Ivy Tech Community College and Vincennes University supply the bulk of in-state volume, alongside heavy internal migration from IU's regional campuses (IU Indianapolis, East, Kokomo, Northwest, South Bend, Southeast). Out-of-state flow leans on Chicago-area an

name: Iowa
typical: Most admits are Iowa or Illinois community college students with at least 24 semester hours, coming in under a sliding GPA floor Iowa publishes in CDS D8: 2.0 with an AA or AS from an Iowa community college, 2.25 with an AA from an Illinois community college, or 2.50 for everyone else. About seven in ten applicants are admitted, so the real competition is at the college level (Tippie, Nursing, Engineering), not the university gate.
levers: Finish the AA or AS at an Iowa or Illinois community college rather than transferring mid-stream. It lowers your required GPA to 2.0 (Iowa) or 2.25 (Illinois), and per Iowa's articulation policy an AA from any Iowa or Illinois community college clears every Iowa Core general-education requirement except world language and Understanding Cultural Perspectives.

Enroll in the 2 Plus 2 Guaranteed Graduation Plan while you are still at the community college. It locks a four-semester path to the degree in CLAS or Tippie; pair it with Iowa's Online Equivalency Guide and transferiniowa.org to confirm each course transfers before you register for it.
watchouts: Tippie College of Business is a separate direct admission, not a byproduct of being admitted to Iowa: 24 semester hours, a 2.75 prerequisite GPA plus 2.75 UI and cumulative GPA, passing grades in the named prerequisite courses, and no academic misconduct — with extra requirements layered on for the accounting major.

Credit ceilings bind: only 60 semester hours transfer from a two-year institution and you must complete at least 30 hours at Iowa. Separately, D4 requires 24 semester hours to be read as a transfer at all — apply with fewer and you are evaluated as a first-year applicant on high school credentials.
feeders: Kirkwood Community College in Cedar Rapids is the single largest feeder, with Des Moines Area CC, Iowa Central, Eastern Iowa CC, and Hawkeye CC behind it. Iowa also pulls unusually hard from Chicago-area Illinois community colleges (College of DuPage, Harper,

name: Iowa State
typical: Admission is criteria-based rather than competitive: a 2.0 cumulative transferable GPA and good standing clears the university gate, which is why 4 in 5 applicants are admitted. The typical admit is an Iowa community college student arriving with 24+ transferable credits; the real selection happens at the college and major level, not at the university door.
levers: Join the Admissions Partnership Program (APP) at any Iowa community college. It guarantees ISU admission at a 2.0 transferable GPA (calculated across all colleges attended, not just the APP school), gives you a live ISU degree audit while you are still at the CC, and locks your bachelor's degree requirements to your catalog year the way a first-year student's are.

Finish the AA/AS in Iowa and map it through the statewide TransferInIowa transfer-major guides plus ISU's own course equivalency guide before you register each term. The Iowa articulation framework is built so the completed AA clears lower-division general education at the Regent universities, letting you arrive at junior standing and spend all four remaining semesters inside the major.
watchouts: The 80% is the university gate, not your major. Engineering, computer science, and the Ivy College of Business apply their own transfer criteria on top; ISU's CS department routes transfer applicants through its advising center and a separate transfer flowchart rather than publishing a single GPA cutoff. Confirm the major's bar directly before treating the CDS rate as your odds.

ISU accepts a maximum of 65 credits from a two-year institution and requires 32 credits completed at ISU for the bachelor's (CDS D13, D16). Community college hours past 65 do not shorten your time to degree.
feeders: Overwhelmingly Iowa's 15 community colleges through APP, with DMACC and Kirkwood the largest pipelines, plus lateral moves from Iowa and UNI. ISU draws 41% of undergraduates from out of state (CDS F1), so out-of-state community college transfers are routine as

name: Kansas
typical: KU admitted 1,973 of 2,337 transfer applicants for Fall 2025 — an 84.4% rate — so the university-level bar is low and mechanical. The typical admit is a Kansas or western-Missouri community college student with 24+ transferable hours and a 2.5+ GPA, which CDS D7 states is assured admission; the real selectivity sits at the school and major level.
levers: Bank 24+ transferable credit hours with a 2.5+ GPA from a regionally accredited college before applying — CDS D7 makes that combination assured admission, and it also removes the freshman-requirement fallback entirely.

Complete the Kansas Systemwide General Education (KSGE) package at a Kansas public two-year college so gen eds transfer as a block among Kansas public institutions, then use KU's 2-year renewable transfer scholarships, which are awarded on transfer GPA.
watchouts: Assured university admission does not get you into the professional schools — KU Business, Engineering, Journalism, Nursing and Architecture set their own more competitive standards (CDS D11).
Credit ceilings bite: KU caps two-year transfer credit at 75 hours (D13) and requires 30 credits completed at KU for the bachelor's (D16), so stockpiling 90 CC hours wastes roughly a semester.
feeders: Johnson County CC is the dominant feeder (it publishes dedicated KU transfer guides), followed by Kansas City Kansas CC, Butler CC, Cowley College and Wichita-area two-years, plus Washburn and lateral transfers from Kansas State and Wichita State.

name: Lehigh
typical: 804 transfer applicants, 195 admitted, 60 enrolled — a 24.3% transfer admit rate, meaningfully more forgiving than Lehigh's first-year round. Admits clear the CDS D7 minimum college GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, and in practice sit well above it, with at least a full year of college coursework behind them. Men and women were admitted at nearly identical rates (104/452 and 91/352). The steep 195-to-60 yield gap says most admits are cross-applying and choosing elsewhere.
levers: Clear the CDS D4 threshold of 24 completed credit hours before applying — under that, Lehigh requires you to apply as an entering first-year student instead, which drops you into the far larger and far more selective freshman pool.
Apply for spring entry: Lehigh runs a genuine second transfer cycle (11/1 priority, 11/15 close, 12/1 notification, 1/10 reply) against a much smaller pool than the ~800-applicant fall round.
watchouts: Credit ceilings bite: a maximum of 60 credits transfers from a two-year institution (D13), 90 from a four-year (D14), nothing below a grade of C moves at all (D12), and you must still complete 60 credits at Lehigh to earn the bachelor's (D16).

Admission is by college, not to the university at large. Switching into the College of Business afterward runs through Lehigh's internal college-change process, which requires ECO 001 and MATH 021 or 081 completed at C- or better.
feeders: Regional Pennsylvania and New Jersey two-year colleges — Northampton Community College and Lehigh Carbon Community College sit in the Lehigh Valley itself, with Bucks County and northern NJ county colleges close behind — plus students moving up from mid-tier M

name: Loyola Marymount
typical: LMU runs one of the larger transfer operations among California privates: 1,706 admits and 494 enrolled for Fall 2025. CDS D7 lists a 3.00 minimum college GPA, and LMU's own transfer office states the average incoming transfer GPA is about 3.5 — so the typical admit sits half a point above the published floor. The pool is dominated by California community college students, many arriving through a signed district agreement rather than open competition.
levers: The LMU Transfer Admission Agreement (TAG), signed with the Los Angeles Community College District and separately with Santa Monica College. It guarantees fall admission to students who hit the agreed minimum cumulative GPA in LMU-approved coursework and file by the February 1 deadline — the single highest-leverage move for any LACCD or SMC student.

Clear LMU's named course gates before applying: English composition at a U.S. college with a C or better is required of everyone, and College of Business Administration applicants need Business Calculus or Calculus I with a B or higher. The registrar publishes LMU Core equivalency agreements by college, so Core requirements can be finished at the community college.
watchouts: California's Associate Degree for Transfer (ADT) is a CSU-facing guarantee and does not bind LMU as a private university — an ADT alone buys nothing here. The LMU TAG with LACCD or Santa Monica College is the agreement that actually applies.

CDS D13 caps two-year college credit at 60 semester units and D16 requires 30 units in residence; CDS D8 also requires high school transcripts from anyone with fewer than 30 semester hours, so sub-30-unit applicants get read partly on their high school record.
feeders: Los Angeles Community College District campuses under the district-wide agreement, plus Santa Monica College on its own TAG, and Honors Transfer Council of California honors programs that list LMU as a transfer partner. Westside and South Bay LA colleges domin

name: Marquette
typical: Roughly seven in ten transfer applicants are admitted: 340 of 492, with 106 enrolling (a 31% yield, so most admits go elsewhere). By gender, men 240 applied / 155 admitted, women 252 applied / 185 admitted. The clearest real-world benchmark is Marquette's own MATC guaranteed-admission agreement, which sets 24+ transferable credits, a 2.75 cumulative GPA, and no grade below C — treat that as the practical bar for a comfortable admit rather than a bare minimum. Lowest transferable grade is a C (CDS D12). Admission is rolling, so timing moves the odds as much as the transcript does.
levers: Enter through a named guaranteed-admission agreement instead of applying cold. The MATC pathway guarantees admission at a high school diploma or GED, 24+ transferable credit hours completed full-time, a 2.75 cumulative GPA on transferable MATC coursework, and no grade below C. Marquette lists roughly 20 community and technical college partners with guaranteed-admission or articulation agreements and a participation form to opt in — check whether your college is one before you write a single essay.

Apply months inside the rolling window, not at the deadline. CDS D9 lists a July 1 fall priority date, an Aug 10 closing date, and rolling admission — but rolling means files are decided as they arrive, and merit and housing are committed long before August. Spring entry is also open (Dec 1 priority, Jan 1 close, rolling) for every college except nursing.
watchouts: Nursing is the exception to everything above. Transfer students are accepted into the College of Nursing for fall start only — no spring entry — and degree progression requires a 2.500 term and cumulative GPA. The clinical sequence is lockstep, so transferring in without the exact prerequisite courses adds semesters rather than saving them; use Marquette's nursing planning guide to map equivalencies before you enroll in anything.

The 69% rate is university-wide and hides the direct-entry health science tracks. Programs such as physician assistant and physical therapy are built to admit at the freshman level and carry very few transfer seats, so a strong GPA may still meet a closed door in those specific majors. Verify seat availability with admissions for your intended program, not just the university.
feeders: Milwaukee Area Technical College is the named guaranteed-admission partner and the clearest documented pipeline. Marquette states it has partnerships with nearly 20 community and technical colleges carrying guaranteed-admission or articulation agreements — pre

name: Maryland
typical: CDS D2 for Fall 2024: 6,468 transfer applicants, 4,092 admitted, 2,538 enrolled. The typical admit is a Maryland community college student with an AA or roughly 30+ transferable credits and a GPA in the low-to-mid 3s applying to a major outside the Limited Enrollment Programs; UMD's CDS D7 states no minimum college GPA is required but 3.0 is encouraged, and D4 requires 12 attempted semester credits to apply as a transfer rather than a first-year student.
levers: Maryland Transfer Advantage Program (MTAP): enroll in MTAP while at a participating Maryland community college, maintain the required GPA, and submit the UMD transfer application by the March 1 early action deadline (indicating MTAP participation) for guaranteed admission to the university, plus a tuition discount on UMD courses taken concurrently. Decisions come 4-6 weeks after the deadline.

Build the application against ARTSYS (artsys.usmd.edu), Maryland's statewide articulation database: completing an AA plus general education at a Maryland community college transfers gen eds as a block with junior standing, and UMD accepts up to 60 credits from a two-year institution (90 from a four-year), with C- the lowest transferable grade from non-Maryland schools and D- from Maryland schools. Clear each Limited Enrollment Program's named gateway courses with the required grades before applying, since LEP review is course-and-GPA driven.
watchouts: The 63.3% headline is not the rate for the majors most applicants want. Limited Enrollment Programs (Computer Science, Smith School business, engineering, and others) are reviewed separately and far more selectively, and UMD states explicitly that MTAP participants receive no special consideration for LEPs or any specific major - the guarantee is admission to the university only.

Fall closes June 1 but March 1 is the operative early action date: it is the MTAP guarantee deadline, and UMD notifies in mid-April for that round versus late July for later applicants, so a June filing competes for whatever seats and aid remain.
feeders: Overwhelmingly Maryland community colleges feeding through the ARTSYS articulation system and MTAP agreements - Montgomery College and Prince George's Community College are the largest sources, with Anne Arundel, Howard, and College of Southern Maryland also holding transfer agreements. Secondary flows come from other University System of Maryland institutions and from nearby Virginia/DC-area two-year colleges.

name: Michigan State
typical: The admitted transfer is usually a Michigan community college student with 24+ transferable credits and a cumulative GPA at or above the 2.50 floor, with college algebra and first-year writing already done. Roughly four in five applicants are admitted to the university, but that admission is to MSU, not necessarily to the major you named.
levers: Complete the Michigan Transfer Agreement (MTA) 30-credit block at a Michigan community college before you leave — MSU honors it to satisfy its Integrative Studies general-education requirements — and check every single course against transfer.msu.edu first, because MTA completion and MSU course-by-course equivalency are not the same thing.

Use MSU's alternate-major slots deliberately: if your first choice is a restricted major, MSU requires up to two additional choices with at least one non-restricted, and reviews them in the order you list. Ranking a realistic non-restricted third choice converts a major-level denial into a university admit you can build from.
watchouts: Restricted majors run their own secondary admission on top of university admission — Broad College business (hospitality business, for example, wants 28 credits and roughly a 2.90-3.00 core GPA), engineering, and nursing all gate separately. A 2.5 gets you to East Lansing and not into those programs.

Credits past 42 cost you options: at 42+ transferable credits you can no longer select Exploratory, pre-nursing, or pre-veterinary. Only 60 credits transfer from a two-year school (90 from a four-year), so banking a third year at community college wastes both credits and major choices.
feeders: Michigan community colleges dominate, led by Lansing Community College next door, plus Oakland CC, Macomb, Grand Rapids CC, Washtenaw, Henry Ford, and Schoolcraft. Secondary flow is lateral from Michigan four-years — Oakland, Grand Valley, Western Michigan, an

name: Minnesota Twin Cities
typical: Admitted transfers are strong-B to A students who already finished the target college's named prerequisites: UMN publishes average admitted transfer GPAs of 3.74 (Carlson), 3.58 (Biological Sciences), 3.56 (Science & Engineering), 3.45 (Nursing) and 3.38 (Liberal Arts). The overall 53.9% is an all-college blend and materially overstates the odds in the selective colleges.
levers: Complete the full Minnesota Transfer Curriculum (MnTC) at a Minnesota public two-year college — UMN's College of Liberal Arts states a completed MnTC clears the core, theme, and first-year-writing portions of its Liberal Education Requirements, leaving only the writing-intensive piece, so you land with a clean junior-year schedule instead of backfilling gen eds.

Apply to the college whose published average admitted transfer GPA you actually clear (CLA 3.38 vs Carlson 3.74), finish that college's named prerequisites first — calculus plus the physics/chemistry sequence for CSE, the business core for Carlson — then use UMN's internal college-to-college change process once enrolled.
watchouts: Carlson, College of Science and Engineering, College of Biological Sciences, Nursing, Public Health, Medical Laboratory Science and Dental Hygiene admit transfers for FALL ONLY — there is no spring entry, so a missed deadline costs a full year.
Carlson and Nursing have a hard February 1 fall deadline with no space-available extension, while CLA stays open to July 1 and CSE/CBS to June 1 — the single 'UMN deadline' does not exist.
feeders: Minnesota State two-year colleges are the dominant pipeline, especially the Twin Cities metro ones — Normandale, Century, Minneapolis College, North Hennepin, Anoka-Ramsey — with MnTC completion as the standard entry ticket. Secondary streams are lateral trans

name: NC State
typical: CDS D2 for Fall 2025: 5,383 transfer applicants (3,044 men / 2,339 women), 2,405 admitted (1,321 / 1,084), 1,663 enrolled — a 44.7% transfer admit rate. The 2.00 minimum college GPA the CDS reports in D7 is a floor, not the bar: D8 says other requirements 'vary by department,' and competitive admits are NC Community College students who have finished NC State's published courses-required-for-transfer list for their specific major.
levers: C3 (Community College Collaboration): co-enroll at a partner NC community college with NC State advising and a defined path into the university. Join it at the start of your community college coursework rather than applying cold as a transfer two years later.

Finish the AA or AS under North Carolina's statewide Comprehensive Articulation Agreement so general education transfers whole and you arrive with junior standing, then layer NC State's major-specific Transfer Pathway / courses-required-for-transfer list on top of it — the CAA gets you credit, the pathway list gets you the major.
watchouts: Engineering transfers are admitted into the college, not the major — you enter Engineering Undesignated and still have to clear the department's CODA (change-of-degree-audit) GPA to claim a specific engineering degree.
CDS D9 shows a Feb 15 fall priority date and no published closing date, so late fall applications compete for leftover space; spring, by contrast, closes hard on Oct 1.
feeders: Wake Technical Community College is the single largest source, with the rest of the NC Community College System behind it via the CAA and the C3 partnerships; a smaller share transfer laterally from UNC-system four-year campuses.

name: NYU
typical: NYU requires 24+ completed credits and reviews by intended school with program-dependent prerequisites. Fall 2025 ran unusually transfer-friendly — 38.6% vs ~9% for first-years — so treat the rate as a good year, not a promise; 3.5+ with the right prereqs is the standard profile.
levers: School choice is the biggest lever: CAS, Steinhardt, SPS, and Gallatin admit far above Stern/Tisch
Spring and summer entry are both open, giving three cycles per year
watchouts: Stern, Tisch, and Tandon add prerequisites/portfolios and run far below the headline rate
NYU does not meet full need for transfers — aid runs notoriously thin

name: Nebraska
typical: About half of transfer applicants are admitted — meaningfully tighter than UNL's freshman rate, and stable year over year (Fall 2024 was 1,093 admits of 1,958, or 55.8%). The stated bar is 12+ college credits, a 2.0 cumulative GPA and a 2.0 in the most recent term, but UNL's own CDS notes that some colleges have more rigorous requirements than shown.
levers: Cross 24 transferable credits before you apply. Under 24 credits, CDS D8 says you must also satisfy UNL's 16-unit required high school core — one extra community college semester removes an entire second review gate built on your high school record.

Nebraska community college students should target the Nebraska Achievement Community College Tuition Scholarship: it requires over 75% of coursework at a Nebraska community college, a cumulative AND last-term transfer GPA of at least 3.250, and at least 15 Nebraska CC credit hours at the time of application.
